content.value_statement: Teams often struggle to keep tests focused during fast TypeScript changes. This skill guides RED-GREEN-REFACTOR work with practical Node.js patterns.
actual_capabilities: Explain the RED-GREEN-REFACTOR cycle for Node.js and TypeScript features.
Provide AAA test structure examples and clear naming conventions.
Describe unit, integration, contract, and async test patterns.
Show test double patterns such as stubs, mocks, fakes, and spies.
Guide refactoring while keeping the related test set passing.
limitations: Does not run tests or inspect a project by itself.
Examples are generic and may need changes for local frameworks.
Focuses on Node.js and TypeScript, not every language.
Does not replace security, performance, or accessibility testing.

use_cases.title: Add a Feature Safely
use_cases.description: Plan failing tests, implement the smallest behavior, and refactor after the test passes.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Testing
use_cases.description: Use shared naming, AAA structure, and test organization patterns across a Node.js codebase.

use_cases.title: Teach Practical TDD
use_cases.description: Explain test doubles, parameterized tests, async tests, and dependency injection with concise examples.

prompt_templates.title: Start a TDD Cycle
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the tdd-workflow skill to plan a RED-GREEN-REFACTOR cycle for [feature] in a Node.js TypeScript project.

prompt_templates.title: Write First Failing Tests
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the tdd-workflow skill to identify the first failing tests for [behavior], including happy path, edge cases, and error cases.

prompt_templates.title: Design Test Doubles
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the tdd-workflow skill to choose suitable stubs, mocks, fakes, or spies for [module] and explain why each one fits.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor With Tests
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced user improving design after tests pass.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the tdd-workflow skill to review [test plan or module behavior] and propose safe refactoring steps while preserving test coverage.

output_examples.input: Help me test an email validator before implementation.
output: A short behavior list for valid, invalid, empty, and formatted email inputs.
A recommended first failing test and the expected failure reason.
A note to refactor only after the validator behavior passes.

output_examples.input: How should I isolate a service that writes users and logs events?
output: Use a fake repository for stored users and a mock logger for interaction checks.
Keep each test independent with a fresh test context.
Assert observable behavior before checking supporting interactions.

output_examples.input: Review my plan for refactoring after tests pass.
output: A refactoring sequence that keeps the public behavior unchanged.
A list of brittle assertions to replace with behavior-focused checks.
A reminder to rerun the relevant unit and integration tests after each change.

best_practices: Start with one observable behavior and write the failing test first.
Keep test data builders clear and close to the domain language.
Refactor only after the relevant test set passes.
anti_patterns: Testing private state instead of user-visible behavior.
Sharing mutable test state across unrelated cases.
Overusing snapshots for logic that needs explicit assertions.

faq.question: Can this skill run my test suite?
faq.answer: No. It provides TDD guidance and examples. Use your project tools to run tests.

faq.question: Is it specific to Jest?
faq.answer: The examples use Jest style, but the patterns apply to Vitest and similar TypeScript test runners.

faq.question: Does it create production code?
faq.answer: It can guide minimal implementation steps, but it does not generate a full application alone.

faq.question: Can it help with legacy code?
faq.answer: Yes. Use it to characterize current behavior before refactoring legacy TypeScript modules.

faq.question: Does it require database access?
faq.answer: No. Database examples use fake or test dependencies to explain integration testing.

faq.question: Is it safe for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: The skill is documentation-based. The audit found no executable commands or prompt injection evidence.
